item.subject: science
item.stem: Meena visits her uncle's village in the Thar desert and notices that the camels there have wide, padded hooves. Her uncle says this feature helps the camels walk on loose sand without sinking. Which statement best explains why the camel's wide hooves are called an adaptation?

options.A: The wide hooves are a noticeable body part of the camel, and any noticeable body part is an adaptation.
options.B: The wide hooves are a special feature that helps the camel survive in the sandy desert region where it lives.
options.C: The wide hooves help the camel walk faster than other animals, so they are an adaptation for all regions.
options.D: The wide hooves look different from the hooves of horses, so they are counted as an adaptation.
